Utilities racing to build more fossil-fuel generation, including to meet soaring demand from AI data centers, and the companies selling them fossil fuels.

text:
AI presents both massive opportunities and catastrophic risks. Meeting this moment will require focused, thoughtful, data-driven responses that keep pace with rapidly evolving technology.

Thank you to @RonConway and @JayCarney for their leadership in launching Project Blueprint and bringing policymakers and innovators together to find a better path through the perils and promise of AI.

quoted.text:
After such a consequential week for AI, with the leading labs demonstrating real progress, today's news feels especially timely: @SVAngel is launching Project Blueprint, a comprehensive effort to forge consensus among industry leaders and lawmakers around durable solutions to the hardest AI policy challenges so that all Americans can benefit from AI's opportunities. And we've brought on @JayCarney to run it. https://t.co/0qb7MIGknd

We are encouraged by the reaction of Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Demis Hassabis to the launch of Project Blueprint:

Sam Altman, co-founder and CEO of OpenAI: "We have before us a technology of immense and still-unfolding wonder. I believe AI has the power to heal people, to discover cures and to deliver abundance on a scale the world has never known before. But we need a way for the world to build trust in the technology so that we can all get to share these benefits. National safety requirements for the most capable systems are a great first step, ideally building towards a global framework for advanced AI models. I’m glad Ron is bringing the people building AI and policymakers together to help move that work forward.”

Dario Amodei, CEO and co-founder, Anthropic: "AI is advancing faster than our institutions can adapt, and the most important decisions about how it is developed and deployed will be made in the next few years. If those decisions are to serve the public, they can't rest with AI companies alone. Industry and policymakers need to work through them together, with an honest, shared understanding of what these systems can do. We're glad to support Project Blueprint's effort to make that possible." 

Demis Hassabis, chairman and co-founder of Google DeepMind and the chief scientist of Alphabet: "We have long said that AI development needs to be both bold and responsible. We support bringing industry and lawmakers together around public policies that promote both innovation and safety."

text:
The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) technology comes with serious risks. If the world continues to adopt AI at a rapid rate without greater safety controls and slower development, incidents could threaten our security and safety. As leading artificial intelligence companies voice their concerns on the dangers that AI presents, Congress must act proactively to ensure proper guardrails are put in place to protect our country and humanity and ensure that AI deployment is safe, stable, and secure.

Unfortunately, President Donald Trump refuses to lead on this issue and Speaker of the House Mike Johnson blocked a bipartisan AI task force that would address the same concerns being raised by AI CEOs. The United States Congress must take decisive action now to slow AI development by coordinating both across the aisle and with our global partners to set strong safety standards and guardrails for this technology while preserving American innovation and competitiveness. 
 
Although Congress is working on solutions, we must do more to ensure that the necessary conversations are taking place so that safeguards and standards can be put in place to protect us. I do believe that AI can improve the quality of our lives. However, the benefits of AI will only outweigh its potential threats if we take the deliberate time and care to ensure responsible AI development and to get it right.

text:
Earlier today, I was leaving a Science Committee hearing, standing up for science to address climate change, when I was once again followed, shouted at, and harassed by two rogue paid actors attempting to intimidate.

Let me be clear: I have always wanted the wars in the Middle East to end. I believe in a two-state solution that gives Israelis and Palestinians peace, security, dignity, and a home. People are free to disagree with me, challenge me, and protest my positions. That is democracy.

But disagreement is not license for intimidation or harassment.

I’m not on the ballot anymore. So, what exactly are we accomplishing by continuing to tear each other apart? There is too much at stake to spend our energy villainizing people on our own side or like me who are not coming back to Congress.

We should be putting our energy into protecting Social Security, defending voting rights, lowering costs, standing up for science, and defending the people who sent us here.

Disagreement is democracy. Intimidation isn’t.

Let’s get back to work.

text:
Today, I voted no on the Clarity Act, legislation meant to regulate cryptocurrency in America.

The ethics provisions in this bill are simply too thin. President Trump, his children, and his Cabinet are making billions of dollars in the crypto space, in part from bilking everyday Americans out of their hard-earned money. I cannot in good conscience vote for any legislation that codifies that behavior from public officials. Not for President Trump or Secretary Lutnick today, nor for any Democrat who may take advantage of it in the future.

On the national security front, there is more to be done to make sure we have the tools in place to stop money laundering and shut down funding avenues for terrorists and nations like North Korea and Iran. This was essential after 9/11 and remains essential to keep Americans safe.

And as of now, our agencies, including the CFTC, lack the necessary oversight and staffing to implement this legislation, and that should be addressed.

There are strong, bipartisan provisions in this bill that could serve as the foundation for a new attempt at providing the crypto industry with the guardrails it needs. I believe that the U.S. should lead the world in cryptocurrency innovation, but we need to get it right. I remain open-minded to that work ahead.

On Friday, Montgomery County rededicated an extraordinary 9/11 memorial by sculptor Sassona Norton — two hands clasping a steel beam from the North Tower of the World Trade Center.

This beautiful sculpture was moved to Elmwood Park, with the help of many dedicated volunteers, to be more accessible to Montco residents.

25 years after 9/11, it is our duty to bring the horrors of that day, and the profound sense of unity that followed, to the forefront of our collective memory.

When Hurricane Lowell hit, one of the only voices Kauaʻi could still hear was KKCR, their community radio station.

Through power and internet outages, KKCR stayed on the air, sharing emergency updates and helping people find food, water, and help. After Trump pushed Republicans to cut public broadcasting funding, KKCR lost $83,000. Congress must restore funding for this critical lifeline  because when disaster strikes and every other line of communication goes dark, Kauaʻi needs KKCR to be there.

text:
This morning, I joined @CHCI’s 2026 Leadership Conference to close out a discussion on economic competitiveness and the future of American trade.

CHCI brings together Hispanic leaders, students, policymakers, and businesses to talk about the issues affecting our communities and our economy.

Laredo is at the center of that conversation. As the nation’s busiest land port of entry, our community sees firsthand how trade policy affects jobs, prices, investment, and the movement of goods across North America.

I spoke about the need for predictable trade rules, a strong USMCA, and continued investment in our ports so businesses can plan, workers can compete, and North America can remain competitive.

Thank you to CHCI for bringing these voices together and continuing to develop the next generation of Hispanic leaders.

Today at the National Museum of African American History and Culture, I joined with Congresspersons Jonathan Jackson and Melanie Stansbury, Bishop William J. Barber II, Pastor Robert Turner, other faith leaders, advocates gathered again for a call to action. Our message to the Trump administration was clear, and it centered on protecting the Smithsonian Museum and the full and honest telling of American history.

That history should not be under attack because its truths are difficult or inconvenient. Preserving it requires vigilance, commitment and a willingness to speak up when the record is being diminished or erased.

Without reservation our history must be preserved, protected and told truthfully.

And for those who need a reminder: If you attempt to erase it, we will replace it!"

#HandsOffOurHistory #AmericanHistory
#Smithsonian
#CBC

Cancer patients in South Texas should have access to the latest treatments and clinical trials, regardless of where they live.

I spoke with Federico Juarez IV from Laredo and @AmericanCancer about federal funding for cancer research and prevention, as well as efforts to make clinical trials easier for patients to access.

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, I have supported federal investments in the NIH, National Cancer Institute, ARPA-H, and CDC cancer programs that help advance research, improve early detection, and develop new treatments.

We also discussed the Clinical Trial Modernization Act, which would help reduce barriers that can keep patients, especially those in rural communities, from participating in clinical trials.

I will continue working to support cancer research and make sure patients in South Texas have access to the latest treatments and clinical trials

text:
When a hurricane, flood, or other disaster hits, families and local governments need federal assistance to reach them as quickly as possible.

I met with @fema Administrator Cameron Hamilton to discuss disaster response and recovery and how FEMA can better support communities when they need help.

We talked about Individual Assistance for families, Public Assistance for local governments, hazard mitigation funding, and ways to reduce delays in getting federal resources where they are needed.

Texas recently submitted a disaster declaration request, and while some assistance has been authorized, communities still need clarity on remaining needs, timelines, and available support.

Texas communities know how devastating natural disasters can be. I will continue working with FEMA and local officials to make sure communities have the resources they need to prepare, respond, and recover.
